title: BENZ SPJ — VYGER Atlantis / VYGER INERTIAL / ART USB Phono Plus — Hi Fidelity Milan

setup.measurement_location: Hi Fidelity Milan — CHARIO Academy room
setup.adjustments_for_measurement: none; setup measured as found, per measurer

harmonic_reliability.quality_note: Steady during recording. Suitable for setup guidance.

interpretation.summary: Measured as found in the CHARIO Academy room at Hi Fidelity Milan, with no setup adjustments: the BENZ SPJ / VYGER Atlantis / VYGER INERTIAL / ART USB Phono Plus chain averaged 33.33 RPM (−0.01%), with 0.032% DIN-shaped wow and flutter, 27.4 dB average separation and +0.49 dB channel balance. Harmonics were steady during recording. The measurer reports a successful 100 µm tracking-ladder pass and credits the new INERTIAL tonearm as a major contributor to that performance.
interpretation.recommendation: Preserve this unchanged show-room setup as a baseline. A longer documented repeat could explore the 3.03 dB directional separation difference and extend the tracking-ladder observation.
interpretation.tonearm_context: The newly identified VYGER INERTIAL tonearm was central to the tracking demonstration. Michelangelo Canonico attributes much of the successful 100 µm tracking-ladder performance to this new arm, with no setup adjustments made for the session. The supplied INERTIAL manual describes a movable counterweight supported by an air bearing and controlled laterally by magnetic forces. The manufacturer explains that this arrangement allows freer lateral movement when following record eccentricity. It also describes a shorter counterweight-to-pivot distance intended to reduce vertical inertia. These design features provide context for the strong tracking demonstration; this single session did not isolate the arm’s contribution from that of the cartridge and turntable.

provenance.data_entry_method: Values transcribed verbatim from the original PDF report; rounded differences are preserved rather than recalculated.
provenance.raw_audio_note: No raw test-record audio is included.
provenance.setup_metadata_source: The PDF title identifies BENZ SPJ and VYGER Atlantis and the input field reports USB Audio CODEC. The measurer supplied the ART USB Phono Plus identity, show and room, no-adjustment context, 100 µm ladder pass and acknowledgement. On 7 October 2026, the measurer identified the new tonearm through the supplied INERTIAL manual and attributed much of the tracking performance to it.
known_limitations: A quick show-room capture with no setup adjustments, according to the measurer; not an optimised or controlled laboratory comparison.
Stylus, loading, tracking force, alignment, anti-skate, test-record identity and track, interface routing and gain, capture settings, software versions, timezone and repeat count were not supplied.
The 100 µm tracking-ladder pass is a measurer-reported session observation outside the source PDF; frequency, record and pass criterion were not supplied.
Reported differences retain source precision and may differ from subtraction of rounded channel values.
No before/after tonearm comparison was supplied; the arm’s major contribution is the measurer’s assessment, supported by design context from the manual rather than an isolated causal measurement.
provenance.photo_treatment: Original event photograph preserved. Web image is a resized format conversion with no AI retouching or background replacement.
